_comment: Differences between the two implementations of the skill frontmatter contract that are
DELIBERATE, each with the reason it is deliberate.
.github/scripts/lint_skills.py      the repo's own gate, hardcoded, run over the live
catalogue and the marketplace plugin tree
skill-schema.json                   the shipped, generalised contract as data
check_lint_parity.py compares five properties across the two. Anything that differs and is
not registered here fails. Two rules, both learned elsewhere in this repository:
- 'reason' is required, and should explain why the two SHOULD differ, not why they do.
- an entry whose two sides have converged also fails. An exemption for a divergence that
no longer exists is one nobody granted, and it will silently absorb the next divergence
on the same property. Same rule the practice gate applies to sweep_exclusions.
'repo_side' and 'toolkit_side' record the divergence AS MEASURED. They are compared against
the live values, so widening a required-field list does not slip in under an entry written
for a different field. Order is not compared for list-valued properties; membership is.
This registry does NOT resolve the drift -- it declares it. Making the repo-side lint match
the schema would re-baseline a gate that currently holds a working catalogue, which is a
separate decision with its own evidence.

exceptions.reason: The repo side requires `name`; the shipped schema declines to. In a personal or project skill `name` is a display label and the command comes from the DIRECTORY, so a mismatch mislabels rather than misroutes -- verified 2026-08-16 and recorded in SKILL-FRONTMATTER.md. Requiring it is therefore a house rule, not a platform rule. This repository is a curated catalogue and legitimately wants every skill to carry one; the schema ships to recipients who must not be handed a house rule dressed as a platform constraint. Both profiles still enforce name-matches-directory WHEN PRESENT, so the only real difference is whether an absent `name` fails.

The shipped list is the broader one, and it is broader on purpose: a required field filled with `TODO`, `N/A` or `-` is not a filled field either, and a recipient's tree will contain all three. The repo side is narrower and additionally treats an empty value as unfilled through a separate emptiness test, which is why the empty string appears in its literal and not in the schema's. Widening the repo-side list is safe but is a behaviour change on every skill in the live catalogue (32 of them, 2026-08-16), so it belongs to whoever is prepared to read the resulting failures rather than to this gate.

`skill_id` and `slash_command` are this repository's LOCAL PLUGIN EXTENSIONS. Neither is among the six frontmatter fields accepted outside the CLI, so a file carrying one fails packaging with a hard error rather than having the key ignored -- which is why the shipped schema must not demand them, and treats `slash_command` as checked-when-present instead. The repo side requires both because its plugin tree is generated by its own generator and every file in it carries them, so the local convenience is already paid for here; the portability it costs is a cost this repository has accepted and a recipient has not. `name` agrees on both sides: in a plugin skill it sets the last segment of the command, so requiring it is a platform rule there rather than a house rule.
